published_prior_art.cite: BanKedagni2022 gives valid normalized SDC/LEI outer bounds, not an exact-support eligibility characterization.

BanKedagni2022 states its SDC bounds as nonparametric bounds and leaves sharpness open in the corroborating arXiv version; Park2025 is an unpublished SSRN WIP with no theorem text inspected and was not used to negate novelty.
BaiEtAl2026 treats total-variation closure and testing for unknown-coefficient linear systems, but not this SDC support-filtered set map or its explicit two-point family.
KaidoMolinariStoye2019 provides asymptotically valid calibrated projection for moment models; primitive Hoeffding projection is a conservative specialized construction.
ChoRussell2024 studies perturbed-LP inference, but does not supply a completion-slack adaptation frontier for a component-disappearing exact set.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 4 / def:projection-region
soundness_flags.one_line: The union ranges over undefined maps p(P') and omega(P'), and H_n permits p_j=0 although the downstream m_j=omega_j/p_j conditional mean is undefined; define the primitive-to-set extension directly and restrict or specify zero-mass cells.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Official article abstract and bibliographic record, pp. 477-493
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The primary publication exists at the cited venue and states that it derives nonparametric ATE bounds under same-direction correlation, with an identified set in intersection-bound form.

Theorem 3.1 gives uniform asymptotic validity for calibrated-projection confidence sets under its regularity assumptions; it is not a finite-sample Hoeffding theorem for the proposed support-filtered map.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, 2024, DOI 10.1080/07350015.2023.2203768
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited Cho--Russell paper exists at the claimed venue and year; its stated topic is inference for functionals of set-identified parameters defined by linear moments.
The paper characterizes total-variation closure of the null and develops tests for linear systems with unknown coefficients, rather than the proposed exact-support SDC closure.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define p(P') and omega(P') as primitive cell-mass functionals and define the candidate sharp set directly in (p,omega), with an explicit convention or exclusion for zero candidate masses; then restate Theorem 4 over that well-defined image.

Add a second named imperfect-IV comparator or promote the sharpness claim to a generic class of normalized multiplier outer bounds, proving strict inclusion on an observable nondegenerate region rather than only at P-star.
Develop the OEQ into a concrete slack-indexed upper/lower rate statement, naming the loss, a rate regime in kappa_n, and a candidate perturbation or testing construction.

recommended_next_step: Repair the primitive projection-region definition, then advance the field-tier exact-support sharpness kernel to Stage 0.
